newsitem.title: USA: FINEX to launch Australian, New Zealand dlr future.
newsitem.headline: FINEX to launch Australian, New Zealand dlr future.

text.p: FINEX, the financial products division of the New York Cotton Exchange, is to start trading in two new currency futures contracts on May 1 - an Australian/U.S. dollar contract and a New Zealand/U.S dollar contract.

"The new Australian and New Zealand contracts are particularly intriguing in that they can be traded to create a cross Aussie/Kiwi position which has attracted a lot of attention in cash foreign exchange markets in recent years," FINEX vice president of marketing, Charles Minaar said.
"The launch of these two futures contracts constitutes the third set of new FINEX currency contracts launched in the early part of 1997," FINEX vice president of marketing, Charles Minaar said.

Other new currency contracts, out of 11 to be launched by FINEX this year, were the Deutsche mark/Spanish peseta cross rate contract, the British pound/Swiss franc cross, the British pound/Japanese yen cross and the U.S. dollar/South African rand contracts.

"The introduction of the Malaysian ringgit, Indonesian rupiah, Thai baht, Singapore dollar and Canadian dollar against the U.S. dollar will be the next step in increasing the already wide range of currency products traded on FINEX," he said.
FINEX first introduced futures contracts on several currency cross rates and U.S. dollar currency pairs with the opening of its FINEX Europe trading floor in Dublin in June 1994.
"With trading facilities in Europe and the U.S., open outcry access is provided during the Asian, European and U.S. trading day," Minaar said.
